title: Independent contribution and objective
summary: Recoverable Safety Journals for Crash-Consistent AI-Mediated Health-State Mutations. Recoverability is a safety property of the *joint* clinical row, immutable decision lineage, and asynchronous side-effect record, not just of one database commit. Define a recoverable outcome function that returns COMMITTED, REJECTED, or INDETERMINATE until reconcilable ground truth exists.
procedure: Write full claim-to-prior-work falsification matrix, target reader, non-overlap and one paragraph scope. Indicate truly distinct endpoint and strongest competing explanation.
positive: Contains specific candidate mechanism vs 3 strong baselines.
negative: Overlapping published GLHS result as new evidence.
pass_gate: Signed scope register and go/no-go decision
risks: If a correctly engineered PostgreSQL transaction + outbox + idempotent consumer achieves the same invariants and equal/better recovery cost, discard the new mechanism superiority claim.
Very high novelty bar, deadline nearly immediate. Do not submit a routine outbox implementation as a breakthrough.
research_gap: Transactional outbox and database WAL already give crash-safe writes; the unresolved issue worth testing is whether an AI proposal lineage and user-visible decision stay consistent across crash windows and arbitrary duplicate deliveries. Without a new counterexample to a careful outbox baseline, this is an application paper, not a DSN A contribution.
candidate_mechanism: A reconciler checks a versioned decision receipt against the committed row, independent outbox receipt and consent epoch. Invalid/ambiguous evidence never becomes a positive outcome; retry decisions are keyed to immutable operation IDs.
strong_baselines: DB transaction only + fire-and-forget side effect
PostgreSQL atomic write + transactional outbox + idempotent consumer
Durable workflow/saga with compensation and stable operation IDs
primary_metrics: orphan clinical writes per independent history
rqs: RQ1: Across crash cut points, are there executions where the clinical state, decision receipt, and outbox state disagree after bounded recovery?
RQ2: Under at-least-once replay and concurrent consent revocation, does recovery preserve idempotence, causal order, and correct INDETERMINATE labels?
RQ3: What is the added durable-write, p99 latency and recovery-time cost compared with transactional outbox and durable workflow baselines?
falsification: If a correctly engineered PostgreSQL transaction + outbox + idempotent consumer achieves the same invariants and equal/better recovery cost, discard the new mechanism superiority claim.

procedure: Write full claim-to-prior-work falsification matrix, target reader, non-overlap and one paragraph scope. Indicate truly distinct endpoint and strongest competing explanation.
